text:
alex: Heads up — our replay harness numbers look ~1.7-2x slower than the synthetic long-context runner for prefill-dominant traces. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

maria: Yep, saw it after the last kernel selector tweak. Replay p95 for 8k prefill jumps a lot.

sam: FWIW replay mixes conversation ids which lowers KV cache reuse. Synthetic test replays the same convo many times so prefix caching is way better.

jordan: Also check batching heuristics. The runtime currently stops continuous batching when inflight prefix > 512 tokens, so long prefill sequences force smaller batches. That kills throughput even if token kernels are fast.

liz: Ran a quick like-for-like to compare. Same model, same machine, identical seq histogram fed into synthetic vs replay harness (only client-id distribution changed). Results below.

liz: ```
# test command (local harness)
./bench --model redwood-13b --seq-hist seq_hist.json --clients 128 --duration 300 
# results (tokens/s, p50/p95 latency ms)
synthetic: throughput=115k tok/s, p50=42ms, p95=140ms
replay:    throughput=62k  tok/s, p50=85ms, p95=410ms
kv_hit_rate: synthetic=78%, replay=23%
```

alex: Wow the kv_hit_rate gap explains a lot. 23% is brutal for prefill-heavy.

maria: There's another angle — kernel selection is flipping to fallback attention for sequences that cross 4096->8192 boundary in replay. Selector thresholds are heuristic-based on avg seq; replay's sequence mix causes more worst-case picks.

jordan: Right — kernel selector currently uses histogram-percentile(90) to pick the attention kernel and quant path. For replay mixes with heavy tail the selector picks safe kernels (more memory / slower) because of a few long traces. We should try percentile=99 for like-for-like long-context experiments, or force a kernel via env flag.

sam: Proposal: two short experiments
- sticky-client replay (assign stable client ids so prefix reuse improves)
- forced-kernel runs (force int8-attn/kernelX)
Will help isolate KV-caching vs kernel-selection vs batching.

liz: I can run both. Quick config snippet to reproduce sticky clients:```
{
  "replay": { "clients": 128, "sticky_client_ids": true, "client_interleave": "none" },
  "batching": { "continuous_max_prefix": 8192 }
}
```

perf-bot: Regression alert: build 2026.3.42 changed kernel-selector heuristics (PR #1127). Impact label: long-context throughput.

alex: Good catch. Next steps: liz run sticky-client + forced kernel, maria dump selector decisions and per-batch kernel tags, sam add KV hit-rate per-client instrumentation, jordan test continuous_max_prefix=8192 in staging. I'll open an ops ticket with checklist.

maria: One more note — profiling trace from the replay run shows heavy GPU time in kernel "attn_fallback_fwd" instead of "attn_opt_int8" for segments >4096. Dump excerpt:```
[profiler] batch_id=2345 kernel=attn_fallback_fwd ms=1340 (55%)
[profiler] batch_id=2346 kernel=attn_opt_int8     ms=420  (18%)
```

sam: If we increase continuous_max_prefix we may regain batching but memory pressure increases. Need to simulate memory churn with our synthetic mem-sanitized traces.

liz: I'll post results in this thread when done. For now, leaning towards: most of the delta = KV reuse gap (~1.8x) and a chunk from kernel-selector fallback (~1.2x). Batching adds ~1.1x depending on config.

alex: Perfect. Keep it short and concrete in the ops ticket. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
